This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley establishes the Governor's Prescription Drug Abuse Prevention Council to develop a comprehensive State Plan to combat and prevent prescription drug abuse.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley, due to the result of the winter storm, which occurred between February 11, 2014 and February 13, 2014 suspends the requirements relating to length, width, weight, load, and time of service for commercial and utility vehicles carrying unmanufactured forest products, including but not limited to timber, timber byproducts, logs, woodchips, and vegetative debris, through and throughout South Carolina and direct the South Carolina Department of Transportation and the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, and the State Transport Police as needed, to comply with this order.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley releases the Interim Governance Committee from any further responsibilities related to the operation of South Carolina's statewide Health Information Exchange and declares that Executive Order 2009-15 is canceled, rescinded, and from this date declared null and void.
This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley appoints John H. Bartell, Jr. as Sheriff of Williamsburg County.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares February 11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 18, and 19, 2014 to be legal holidays for banks and savings and loan institutions in the State of South Carolina due to hazardous weather. — Severe storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley excuses all state employees absent from work as directed on February 11, 12, 13, and 14, 2014 due to the closing of state offices caused by hazardous weather conditions. — Severe storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley suspends Michael L. Johnson from
the office of Sheriff of the Williamsburg County until such time as he shall be formally
acquitted or convicted.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares that a state of emergency no longer exists and hereby declare that Executive Order 2014-11 is canceled and rescinded. — Severe storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley suspends the federal rules and regulations that restrict certain size and weight and time of service limits in order to ensure the delivery of equipment, materials, services, supplies, food, and other items in response to winter storm operations throughout South Carolina and direct the South Carolina Department of Transportation and the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, and the State Transport Police as needed, to comply with this order.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley orders the Department of Public Safety in conjunction with the Department of Transportation to waive certain size and weight restrictions andpenalties under the provisions set out in 23 CFR 658.17(h) and S.C. Code Sections 57- 3-130(8)(1) and 56-5-?0(A) due to freezing weather..

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares that a State of Emergency exists in South Carolina. Accordingly, I direct the South Carolina Emergency Operations Plan be placed into effect and require state agencies to support the responsibilities and tasks therein.  She further orders the utilization of the South Carolina National
Guard's personnel with appropriate equipment, at the discretion of the Adjutant General
Executive Order 2014-11 and in coordination with the South Carolina Emergency Management Division, to take necessary and prudent actions to assist the citizens of this state. — Severe storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley orders a new election to be held for the City of Belton on April 22, 2014 and designate the City of Belton Election Commission to perform the necessary official duties pertaining to the election to declare the result.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares January 28, 29, and 30, 2014 to be legal holidays for banks and savings and loan institutions in the State of South Carolina due to severe weather.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley directs that all state employees absent from work as directed on January 28, 29, and 30, 2014 due to the closing of state offices caused by hazardous weather conditions are hereby granted leave with pay. — Severe storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares that a state of emergency no longer exists and hereby declare that Executive Order 2014-06 is canceled and rescinded. — Severe storms--South Carolina

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley suspends the federal rules and regulations that limit the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive, in order to ensure the uninterrupted supply of fuel oil, diesel oil, gasoline, kerosene, and LPG throughout South Carolina.
This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declare that a State of Emergency exists in South Carolina due to severe winter weather between January 28, 2014 and January 30, 2014.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares a State of Emergency for the purpose of suspending the federal rules and regulations that limit the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive in order to ensure the uninterrupted supply of residual oils for industrial use throughout South Carolina.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares a State of Emergency for the purpose of suspending the federal rules and regulations that limit the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive in order to ensure the uninterrupted supply of liquid petroleum gas throughout South Carolina, Georgia, and North Carolina.
This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley grants leave with pay to state employees in Dorchester and Fairfield Counties for the hours missed due to the delay of State offices on January 7, 2014.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley determines that an emergency exists in the State South Carolina for the limited purpose of complying with the declaration of emergency in the State of Georgia and accordingly direct the South Carolina Department of Transportation and the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, and the State Transport Police as needed, to suspend the federal rules and' regulations that limit the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive, in order to ensure the uninterrupted supply of liquid petroleum gas to the State of Georgia.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley determines that an emergency condition exists in the State of West Virginia and accordingly directs the South Carolina Department of Transportation and the South Carolina Department of Public Safety, and the State Transport Police as needed, to suspend the federal rules and regulations that limit the hours operators of commercial vehicles may drive, in order to ensure the uninterrupted supply of emergency water to the State of West Virginia.
This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley permits the National Guard to be made available to the City of Georgetown for the removal of debris from the Sampit River.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley direct all state agencies to comply with South Carolina Code Section 1-11-58 and Proviso 118.2 by completing directives dealing with state owned real estate.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares that an emergency exists as a result of fire destruction to the historic district in the City of Georgetown for the purpose of directing the Department of Commerce to undertake actions to allocate funds from the Community Development Block Grant to be used for economic recovery in the Georgetown community.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley declares that an emergency exists as a result of the damage caused by heavy rains at the Jones Mill Road Bridge in Pickens County and direct the South Carolina Department of Transportation to undertake actions to replace the collapsing bridge to ensure the safety and well-being of the traveling public.
This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley appoints Robert I. Lee as Sheriff of Chesterfield County.

This executive order by Governor Nikki Haley suspends Sanford "Sam" Marion Parker, Jr. from the office of Sheriff of the Chesterfield County until such time as he shall be formally acquitted or convicted.
